races.name: Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Recon Mission
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a placed effort at 5f on good last time, handled similar conditions once in five attempts (1P from 15 sim-going runs so limited fast-ground record), and at ten years old George Downing needs to find a clear run late — feasible only if Hakin Adraar sets a strong enough tempo to bring the closer into play.
runners_data.comment: Recon Mission has placed second and third in recent starts and shapes as a clear threat here, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the worry is that he's been winless in his last five starts and hasn't run for 46 days.

runners_data.name: Diomed Spirit
runners_data.note: Second last time at 5f on good ground suggests the trip and conditions suit, though flat-profile hold-up style means Charles Bishop will need a proper gallop to deliver from off the pace — Brighton's sharp finish can reward a late burst but the lone-leader scenario may leave this one with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Diomed Spirit arrives as the top-rated runner in the field, and his second last time out — off a 39-day break carrying 135 lb from stall one — marks him as a genuine threat with distance and going experience in the book; the risk is that he's yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dreambird Dolly
runners_data.note: Solid form record showing 1W and 7P from 13 similar-going runs and a win last time at 5f on good ground makes her the most in-form runner here; her true running style is hold-up, pushed forward on the map only because the field is overloaded with hold-up types — Donagh Murphy (7) will need to find a prominent slot early to exploit that recent winning form.
runners_data.comment: Dreambird Dolly has experience of today's trip and going, and consecutive runner-up finishes show she's in decent nick, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 134 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Stapleford Park
runners_data.note: 109 days off the track is the immediate flag, and a hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield position on the map due to the field's style distribution — Attwater's 14-day strike rate of 1/14 does not inspire confidence after this layoff, and the stamford-like form figures away from good ground suggest conditions here are a step up in suitability.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 109 days off, Stapleford Park does have experience over today's trip and a second two starts back to suggest some ability, though sevenths at two of his last four outings are hard to ignore from stall two carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good last time and gets a weight break at OR 50 for Tony Carroll, but this is a drop to 5½f and his true hold-up style is mapped to midfield only because there is no room at the rear — William Carson will need to adapt his ride, and the shorter trip may catch him out before he can deploy his finish.
runners_data.comment: Washington Heir showed a win two starts back, and that third last time out keeps him lightly respected, but he ranks last on our figures in a field of seven and his official mark of 50 leaves little margin — hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Reporter
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) suggests a horse that needs settling, and his true hold-up profile is squeezed into midfield solely by the volume of hold-up types in this field; Hodgson's 0/2 T14 figure and a return in just 17 days after a 7th at 5f on good raises questions about whether he is running into peak form at the right time.

runners_data.name: Hakin Adraar
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter and the horse who shapes this entire race — a 3-year-old with a blinker fitted, stepping down sharply from 6-8f trips where he has largely disappointed, and Keenan's task is simply to cross and control; the concern is whether the trip and fast ground unlock something new, or whether his role is purely that of pace-setter for others.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Hakin Adraar nevertheless brings strong fitness credentials just eight days since his last outing, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and steps up on his official mark on our figures — drawn four carrying 127 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Hakin Adraar is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 5½f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Brighton, and with no other genuine pace horse to challenge for the lead, they are virtually guaranteed an uncontested, self-regulated gallop from the outset. Brighton's undulating track and the fast conditions will reward a horse that can control tempo without burning fuel, and Hakin Adraar's recent form over 6-8f suggests they will likely set a measured rather than scorching pace — which could compress the finish rather than guarantee a strong-pace collapse for closers. The majority of this field — Dreambird Dolly, Stapleford Park, Washington Heir, and Reporter — are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the pace map simply because there are more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear. This race shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace in a tracking role or who carry enough finishing speed to close from a true midfield position, with Recon Mission and Diomed Spirit as the natural candidates from out the back if the pace is honest enough.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Hakin Adraar bowls clear uncontested and controls a fair but not punishing tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Hakin Adraar dictates every yard at a measured clip on fast ground, and any horse with enough tactical speed to sit within two lengths of the leader early will be best placed to pounce in the final furlong. This scenario strongly suits horses racing prominently or in a true tracking role who can quicken off a sustainable gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Hakin Adraar sets a genuine clip and the front-end effort tells in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A strong early gallop from Hakin Adraar, combined with the undulating Brighton terrain, brings the hold-up horses into play late as the leader flattens out. True closers who can find a run on the rising finish benefit most, though their ability to reach the front under this scenario hinges on the pace being genuinely strong — which is uncertain given the lone leader profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Muddled Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is too slow and the field bunches, turning the race into a sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A dawdling gallop sees the field compress into a tight group approaching the final bend, reducing the race to a short, sharp dash and negating finishing kick for true hold-up horses. Horses with a high cruising speed and the ability to quicken in tight quarters from midfield gain an edge, though the redistribution of so many hold-up types to midfield means traffic risks are elevated.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Frontrunner Pinged Early
scenarios.trigger: If Hakin Adraar is challenged at the start or outpaced early, losing their uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: Without a clean, uncontested break, Hakin Adraar's race-shaping role disappears and the race becomes chaotic, with multiple horses jostling for cover. This unsettles the entire tempo profile and most likely advantages the horse with the best finishing speed from an undisturbed position, though predicting who benefits is genuinely difficult given the redistribution of so many runners out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Hakin Adraar's gate break is critical — if they miss the kick or are headed early, the entire race shape collapses and the tempo becomes unpredictable for every other runner in the field.

Dreambird Dolly and Washington Heir are both natural hold-up horses placed in midfield on the map; watch whether Murphy and Carson attempt to push forward early, which could create a bunching incident on the short run to Brighton's first bend.

Stapleford Park returns from 109 days off and has no recent turf-good form to draw on — monitor in the paddock and opening exchanges for signs of rustiness that could cause interference from an awkward midfield position.

Recon Mission and Diomed Spirit are the truest hold-up horses in the field and both have the most realistic profile to close late — watch whether Hakin Adraar's gallop is genuinely strong enough by the two-furlong pole to create the gap these two need.

Brighton's undulating track and fast surface can stretch stride patterns significantly in the final quarter-mile; horses carrying 134-135lbs versus the bottom weights at 127-130lbs may feel the weight differential acutely on this terrain in the closing stages.

races.name: JenningsBet In Portsmouth EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
JenningsBet UK's Largest Independent Bookmaker Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Celebrating Ethel
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's seven-year-old has tumbled down to OR 44 and her recent form reads 9-9-6-4 — placed once in 15 similar-going runs with no wins; her natural gear is hold-up, and with the rear slots crowded she is likely to be stuck in a midfield berth she won't naturally settle in, which blunts her already modest claims here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Celebrating Ethel nevertheless ran fourth last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while our rating puts her second among six — the risk is the quick two-day turnaround under a stiff 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Dogged
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has three placed efforts over 10-12f on good going for Carroll, but is being pressed into front-running duties that are entirely foreign to his usual waiting style — the blinkers are noted but the style-fit discount is real, and his last-run prep of just one day raises obvious freshness flags.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a second four starts back, Dogged has experience over today's trip and conditions, and his 48 rating edges his official mark — the main risk is he runs just one day after his latest start.

runners_data.name: Fitzmaurice
runners_data.note: Four-year-old stepping up markedly from his recent 7-8f starts to 10f on a track he hasn't visited, with a form string of 8-7-8-7-6 that shows no signs of a finishing effort anywhere; squeezed out of his natural hold-up slot into midfield, his chances rest almost entirely on a dramatically compressed race that flatters non-progressive types.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with finishes of fifth, eighth, seventh, eighth, sixth and seventh telling a consistent tale of mid-to-tail-of-field efforts, Fitzmaurice is hard to fancy ranked last of six on our figures, though he has run over today's going and returns on a handy 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Myna
runners_data.note: The standout course-and-distance profile in the field — five consecutive runs over 10f on good ground culminating in a win and three places; George Downing takes over from Carroll's usual riders and hood headgear suggests connections are trying to sharpen a horse whose form trajectory is clearly the most encouraging in this race.
runners_data.comment: Myna has been knocking at the door in his last two starts — a second two runs back and a third last time out — and has experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 135 lb from stall six, he holds the strongest rating in the field and returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Outrace
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's six-year-old arrives with a string of double-figure finishes in a 7-8f band, stepping up sharply in trip to 10f on a left-handed undulating course he's never seen; the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag reinforces the concern that a moderate pace over further ground is unlikely to play to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Outrace has struggled for consistency and sits fifth of six on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights; he does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return 13 days ago keeps him fit.

runners_data.name: Thundering Breeze
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's five-year-old is the freshness wildcard — 176 days off and a form string that includes a placed effort at 11f on Stalls turf suggests the stamina and ability are there; the long layoff is the only question mark in an otherwise interesting profile for a steadily-run Brighton mile-and-two.
runners_data.comment: Thundering Breeze has placed — a second three starts back and a third five starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, giving her every chance to threaten here; the main risk is a 176-day absence that leaves fitness the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Dogged is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead from a natural hold-up style, meaning the fractions over this 1m2f Brighton trip on good-to-firm ground are likely to be steady and controlled rather than truly pressured — a false-pace scenario is a genuine risk. With Myna the only true hold-up runner in the field operating from her natural position, the race shape heavily favours horses who can travel comfortably just off a slow gallop and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp sprint. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Celebrating Ethel, Fitzmaurice, and Outrace are all genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield positions they won't naturally surrender, and Dogged itself is a hold-up type pressed into front-running duties it would not ordinarily seek. A steadily-run single-file affair over Brighton's undulating mile-and-two favours prominent stalkers who can sit just behind the crawl and time their run, or a horse like Myna who has genuine form over course-and-distance at this class level and can travel efficiently into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Myna Delivers
scenarios.trigger: If Dogged sets a controlled, uncontested crawl and the field strings out at a moderate tempo from the off.
scenarios.body: Myna's C&D form (1W3P in last five at 10f on good) puts her exactly right for a steadily-run Brighton mile-and-two where the ability to settle and produce a clean finish is decisive; with David Probert riding and Tony Carroll's yard in 5/45 form she has the clearest profile for this race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lay-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering Breeze, returning from 176 days off, has been freshened for this and quickens from just off the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Thundering Breeze's Stalls form over 10-11f and a placed effort at 11f suggest stamina is not an issue, and a freshened horse off a long break can hold fitness advantages over rivals that have been running frequently; Probert going to Myna means this horse is ridden by Seamus Cronin class, but its profile suits a well-run race where class counts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closer Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the midfield-mapped hold-up horses — Celebrating Ethel or Fitzmaurice — travel in their natural rhythm and produce a late run from the pack.
scenarios.body: Both carry the style-fit discount having been pushed out of their preferred rear position, and their recent form (9s, 7s and 8s in the frame columns) offers limited encouragement on a track where course form matters; however a truly dawdling pace that compresses the field could give them a stolen momentum advantage down the hill.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Dogged, despite racing out of role, sets a pace modest enough to conserve energy and the hold-up horses fail to coordinate a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Dogged has three placed efforts in similar going and distance band (10-12f good) and a Tony Carroll yard that clearly knows this horse well enough to put it on the lead; the style-fit discount is significant and the 0W record in similar conditions tempers the case considerably.

watchPoints.text: Dogged has run just one day ago — watch market moves and any late jockey briefing change that might signal connections are cautious about whether he's bouncing off a quick return.
Thundering Breeze's 176-day absence means fitness is genuinely unknown; if he shows signs of blowing in the paddock or early in the race, the stamina assumption over 10f becomes fragile.

With five of six runners carrying a hold-up or redistributed hold-up profile, watch for a walking pace in the early stages — if the tempo is genuinely dawdling, finishing positions in the straight may owe more to positioning luck than style-fit.

Myna's hood (headgear flagged hg:h) is worth tracking in the paddock — if she settles well pre-race it confirms the headgear is doing its job and her C&D form becomes the dominant angle in this field.

Tony Carroll saddles four of the six runners, which creates an unusual dynamic — watch which of his horses (Myna, Dogged, Fitzmaurice, Celebrating Ethel) receives the most support in the market as a proxy for yard confidence.

races.name: Harry Bloom Memorial "Brighton Bullet" Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Quiet Gent
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from a lengthy 295-day absence for Brian Toomey, who has a modest 2/5 recent strike rate; two placed efforts on Good at this trip hint at residual ability, but the long layoff is a significant fitness question and he needs gaps to open from the rear.
runners_data.comment: After a promising third and second in recent starts, The Quiet Gent has experience over today's trip and going, and his rating of 87 marks him out as a lively threat from stall five — though 295 days off the track and a winless recent run of five starts make fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Marcellinus
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's three-year-old has been consistent in 6f good-ground races — four placings and a win from his last five — making his form profile one of the most relevant in the race; Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim is a practical advantage, and if he secures a clean prominent berth without fighting for it, his course profile makes him a live contender.
runners_data.comment: Marcellinus catches the eye with a second two starts back and a winner four starts back, and his consistent recent profile marks him out as the one to beat here. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 94 heads the field, though the 41-day absence is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Tenbob Tommy
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 6f wins on Good and Soft give Sheena West's five-year-old genuine course-and-distance credibility; 116 days off is worth noting, but the form before that break was sharp and Charles Bishop is an experienced Brighton pilot — he needs a clear prominent slot to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Tenbob Tommy has winning form in his last two starts but hasn't run in 116 days, and that fitness query is the key unknown; he has experience over today's trip and going, and carries 138 lb from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Lequinto
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's nine-year-old is a model of consistency with five wins and placings on Good at sprint trips, and his 18-day turnaround is no concern given Carroll's 5/45 recent record suggests he manages his horses carefully; William Carson will hunt a clean passage from his hold-up position and the good ground suits.
runners_data.comment: Lequinto has run over today's trip and going, and his recent form reads well — a winner two starts back and second last time out — though he carries 138 lb from stall seven and our rating of 78 ranks him seventh of ten.

runners_data.name: Bona Fortuna
runners_data.note: 309 days off the track is a major red flag regardless of his placed record on Good ground, and the tongue tie may suggest a previous breathing concern; Michael Appleby's 0/27 T14 record suggests the yard is not in a purple patch, and being squeezed out of his natural prominent role in traffic would leave him with little chance.
runners_data.comment: Bona Fortuna arrives winless in his last five but has rattled up three seconds in recent starts, and experience over today's trip and ground gives him a live chance from stall one; the concern is a 309-day absence alongside a trainer firing at just 3% lately.

runners_data.name: Grey Horizon
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and arrives on the back of a 6f Good win, wearing a visor that likely sharpens his concentration; Christian Howarth's 3lb claim is a bonus for a horse with a clear tactical role, and on genuinely fast ground over a flat 6f he controls his own destiny from the front.
runners_data.comment: Grey Horizon arrives on decent recent form — a winner last time out and a second two starts back — but his speed rating of 72 trails the field, and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, he faces a stiff task at 135 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's four-year-old is a natural hold-up type stepping up from 5f on Good, though his Brighton form over five furlongs has been inconsistent; Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim helps the weight burden but the trip extension and the prominent congestion ahead of him make clean passage uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Cayman Tai arrives in solid nick on 13 days' rest, and with experience of today's trip and going under his belt, his third two starts back underlines his consistency — though that fifth last time out suggests he'll need to find improvement to land the spoils from stall nine carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out in fair recent form, with one win in his last six starts; U S S Charleston has experience of today's trip and going, and at 132 lb from stall 3, his rating of 83 ranks him fifth of ten, with a bit to find.

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's eight-year-old has genuinely won a 6f race on Good ground recently, but his natural inclination is to race prominently — he is mapped to midfield here because the prominent slots are simply oversubscribed in this field, meaning he is unlikely to produce his best from an unfamiliar rearward position; the tongue tie is an additional variable, though his 20-day freshness is fine.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced efforts punctuate his recent record, and he sits last on our figures among ten rivals — hard to fancy at the weights. The winning effort two starts back and a runner-up last time at least show he retains ability, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Duskaura's most recent win came over 6f on Good, so the trip and surface are not concerns for Tony Carroll's three-year-old; however, she is at heart a hold-up horse mapping to midfield under pressure from the field's shape, meaning she may sit between two stools — neither tracking the pace nor arriving with a clear late run — which tempers confidence despite the 13-day sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Duskaura has been largely out of the mix in recent starts — a sixth, sixth, fourth, seventh before winning last time out — making that latest victory hard to read with confidence. Has run over today's trip and going, and 13 days' rest is no concern.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Horizon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride straight to the front from stall six and control tempo on what is effectively a Good to Firm surface — faster than the declared Good. Marcellinus, Tenbob Tommy, Bona Fortuna, and USS Charleston all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the first three slots between the furlong pole and the two-furlong marker, which threatens to produce significant traffic shuffling at a critical stage. The field contains more pace-hungry types than the map can accommodate: Marcellinus and Tenbob Tommy are most likely to actually secure a prominent berth, with Bona Fortuna and USS Charleston at real risk of being squeezed back against their natural inclination. A lone, uncontested leader on ground that suits quick ground specialists, with chaotic midfield scrapping behind, powerfully favours hold-up horses who can produce a clean, late run down the outside — provided they avoid the prominent pile-up — and equally suits any prominent horse that emerges cleanly from the scrum in second or third without burning energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grey Horizon Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Horizon leads unchallenged at a fair-to-strong gallop and the prominent pack scrap without overrunning him.
scenarios.body: Grey Horizon sets fractions suited to himself as the prominent horses burn fuel fighting for positions two through five, leaving clean-finishing hold-up types with ground to make up but potentially clear air; horses that track the leader in the clearest water — most likely Marcellinus or Tenbob Tommy if they secure a clean prominent slot — collect the prize.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Pays Off
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion resolves quickly and one horse slots into an uncontested second without fighting, tracking Grey Horizon before asserting late.
scenarios.body: The horse that avoids the early prominent scrimmage and sits unannoyed in Grey Horizon's slipstream conserves enough energy to challenge over the final furlong on fast ground; Tenbob Tommy's recent course-and-distance winning form and Marcellinus's consistent 6f good-ground placing record make them the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent battle causes a significant pace injection at halfway that burns out the leaders and opens a clear wide lane for a closer.
scenarios.body: A frantic mid-race surge from the prominent pack would stretch the field and leave a late gap for a hold-up horse travelling strongly at the back; Lequinto's five wins and placings on Good and Good to Firm at this trip, combined with William Carson's tactical riding, make him the likeliest beneficiary — The Quiet Gent is a secondary candidate if gaps materialise early enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble produces a genuinely scorching early gallop that burns out Grey Horizon and the entire prominent pack before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Fast ground accelerates the collapse and horses arriving late from the rear find a strung-out field to pick off; this scenario nominally benefits Duskaura and Ancient Times, but both carry STYLE_FIT discounts as true prominent types pushed rearward against their nature, limiting confidence in their ability to execute a genuine hold-up finish.

watchPoints.text: Grey Horizon (Christian Howarth) bursts straight to the front — if he opens up a two-length lead unchallenged before halfway, he has every chance of simply never being caught and the race is effectively over as a tactical contest.

Marcellinus, Tenbob Tommy, Bona Fortuna, and USS Charleston are all targeting the same two prominent positions — a fierce early elbow-battle between the furlong pole and the two-out marker is almost certain, with one or more of these runners losing their position entirely.

Lequinto (William Carson) will be tracking from further back than his rivals — if the prominent scramble does not produce an acceleration that strings out the field, he risks finding a wall of horses with nowhere to go at the two-furlong pole on a track that narrows late.

Bona Fortuna returns from 309 days off the track; watch the pre-race paddock closely — any sign of sweatiness or reluctance to load would confirm the layoff has left him underdone, and his chances depend heavily on finding a smooth prominent berth he may not get.

The going is effectively Good to Firm despite the official Good declaration — horses with a firm-ground concern or who have shown a preference for cut should be downgraded accordingly, and Grey Horizon's recent 6f win on Firm gives him the clearest ground-condition profile in the race.

races.name: Bet In Over 200 Shops Nationwide With JenningsBet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dragon God
runners_data.note: Sharp recent form (1-2-3 in last three starts at five furlongs, good ground) with Charles Bishop in the saddle; steps up to six furlongs here but the hold-up style may not be a concern given the compressed field, and good-ground record of 8/14 is a solid platform — five days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Dragon God won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat from stall 4 carrying 138 lb; the concern is he was only fifth and sixth in two of his last six starts, suggesting consistency could be tested.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who shapes as the race-maker here; Darragh Keenan gets a soft lead on good-to-firm ground he handles (4/15 sim-going), but the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94 flags this as a positional anomaly for the trainer's book, and the 0W form on similar going across 15 runs is a concern for outright winning claims.
runners_data.comment: Mart has placed third two of his last six starts and brings strong recent consistency, running over today's trip and going — a genuine contender from stall one carrying 135 lb, though yet to score in this recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Rajeteriat
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners this hold-up type returning from 46 days off; all recent form is over five furlongs on Southwell and Haydock, and stepping up to six furlongs at Brighton on different ground introduces multiple unknowns — the 10/15 sim-going strike rate is thin and the layoff makes this one to view with caution.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts — third and second in his last three starts back and two starts back respectively — mark Rajeteriat as a genuine contender here, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that last run 46 days ago and a winless recent run of form leave questions over whether he can finally convert.

runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal
runners_data.note: Two wins at six furlongs on good ground give him genuine course-and-distance form credentials, and David Probert's booking is a positive; however, he is a true hold-up horse shuffled into a midfield position in the pace map — his natural rear-of-field style is constrained by an overcrowded back group, and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.93 reflects that.
runners_data.comment: Big Time Rascal won two starts back but was fifth last time out, and while he has run over today's trip and going, that recent dip in form tempers confidence — 132 lb is no featherweight assignment for a horse rated 52.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Chute
runners_data.note: Won over course, distance and going (1/6f/GOO) which is the standout form angle here; Finley Marsh rides and the Jim & Best yard are 0/5 in the past 14 days, but the horse's own record at this track cannot be ignored — that said, as a true closer squeezed into a crowded rear, getting a clear run will be the critical factor.
runners_data.comment: Manhattan Chute returns on fair terms fitness-wise at 24 days, has run over today's trip and going, and that recent win catches the eye, but five defeats around it in his last six starts — including finishes of seventh and ninth — make him hard to fancy ranked sixth of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Recent winner over this exact trip on good ground (1/6f/GOO) and the Gary & Josh Moore yard has hit 2/19 in the past 14 days, providing meaningful trainer momentum; David Probert takes the ride, and although this is genuinely a hold-up horse whose natural position is compromised by the field shape, the course form and yard form combine to keep it relevant.
runners_data.comment: Bated Breeze bolsters his claims with a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while 129 lb is the factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying the lowest weight at 123lbs, trained by John Gallagher who is 2/9 in the last fortnight; form over six furlongs is modest (two finishes of 10th and 6th), and as the lowest-rated runner with the weakest STYLE_FIT score (0.90) in a field where every hold-up horse is fighting for the same late ground, this one faces the toughest ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Kodi K is hard to fancy, though a second two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 38 days off should leave him fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Mart is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f Brighton handicap and, with no serious challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop — a controlled tempo that rewards horses who can sit close to the pace and pick up efficiently. The going is Good to Firm throughout the card (the stated "Good" appears softer than reported conditions), which favours a strong-travelling, prominent style over a come-from-behind approach. Critically, Dragon God, Big Time Rascal, Manhattan Chute, Bated Breeze and Kodi K are all genuine hold-up horses who will be forced into a tighter, more compressed rear group than they would naturally prefer, meaning late kicks will be launched from closer proximity to the pace than usual. This race shape — a lone, unhurried leader, a compressed mid-to-rear pack unable to spread out — decisively favours horses who can track Mart within two or three lengths and pounce in the final furlong, rather than deep closers relying on a strong gallop to pull them through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mart Dictates, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Mart leads without pressure and the race is run at a controlled tempo, allowing a close-tracking runner to collar him late.
scenarios.body: Mart sets a soft, uncontested pace down the Brighton straight and the compressed field trails in a tight bunch two to four lengths adrift; a horse positioned just off the leader has the cleanest passage and the shortest distance to travel when the sprint kicks in at the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mart Gallops Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Mart's uncontested lead proves so comfortable that none of the hold-up horses can close the gap from the compressed rear pack.
scenarios.body: The absence of genuine pressure allows Mart to control the fractions entirely, banking a comfortable lead through the final bend and holding on as the bunched closers run out of real estate on the short Brighton home straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough — perhaps Mart goes quicker than expected — to string the field out and allow a true closer to power through.
scenarios.body: A genuinely fast early tempo exhausts the prominent horses and opens a gap for one of the deeper hold-up runners to rattle through late; the tight Brighton straight compresses margins but a horse finishing on fumes can still be caught.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Compressed Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple hold-up horses attempt to push forward simultaneously, disrupting Mart's comfort and causing a messy, multi-way scramble.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of so many genuine hold-up types into an artificial midfield creates traffic and interference in the straight, and the race devolves into a blanket finish where positional luck and a clear run determine the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Mart is the sole front-runner — if Darragh Keenan elects to go very steady, the controlled tempo will massively compress the field and render the finishing positions almost entirely dependent on where each horse sits turning into the short Brighton straight.

Manhattan Chute's course-and-distance winning form is the single most potent form angle in this field — Finley Marsh must navigate a congested rear group, and a blocked passage at the two-furlong pole would be a serious risk to that chance.

Big Time Rascal and Bated Breeze are both true hold-up horses forced into the same compressed space; with David Probert riding both races (Bated Breeze here, noted elsewhere), traffic interference between these two in the straight is a genuine tactical flashpoint.

Dragon God's progressive recent form (three consecutive placed runs narrowing to a win at five furlongs) masks a question mark over the step to six furlongs — whether Charles Bishop drops in behind Mart early or elects to race prominently will significantly shape whether the trip is an asset or a liability.

The going is reported Good to Firm throughout the Brighton card despite the nominal "Good" classification — horses with strong confirmed form on good-to-firm ground hold a genuine edge over those whose best form has come on softer surfaces.

races.name: Bet Responsibly With JenningsBet Handicap Stakes (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner wearing hood, and with no rivals to push the pace this is a significant tactical advantage at Brighton 7f on Good to Firm; trainer Stuart Williams has solid 14-day figures and this horse ran just two days ago — minimal freshness concern but fitness is obvious, though its recent form string of 75867 and zero wins or places on similar going (0W0P in 3/5 sim-going runs) means it needs to convert a favourable shape it has rarely been handed.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of our assessments among these seven, King Cherry has run over today's trip and going before and carries a workable 135 lb from stall 3; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts and returns just two days after his most recent outing.

runners_data.name: Solar Phoenix
runners_data.note: Has been off 55 days and wears a hood, returning from a break that could mean either freshness or ring-rust; one similar-going hit in four attempts is modest, but Roger Teal's 14-day record of 1/14 is quiet and Dougie Costello brings quality in the saddle — style is unclassified (U) so could slot anywhere from prominent to midfield.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and yet to make the frame in recent efforts, Solar Phoenix does at least bring distance experience to this assignment; carrying 134 lb from stall six, however, with our rating suggesting he falls short of the top pair here, he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Pennine Way
runners_data.note: Runs prominently for Jack Channon and George Bass and should slot in as the most natural tracker behind King Cherry; the 17-day turnaround is routine and two placed efforts on similar going give some confidence, though a form string of 4-6773 shows consistency rather than winning threat.|
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and lightly fit at 17 days, Pennine Way brings distance and going experience into this, and her rating of 61 offers a small edge — though she remains yet to win in her last five starts, stall two could at least ensure a clean break.

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: The most compelling on-form horse in the race with two recent wins at 7f on Good ground; Myla Coppins claims 5lb and Tony Carroll's yard is firing at 5/45 in 14 days — hold-up style suits a true pace collapse, and seven of fifteen similar-going runs have resulted in a place, giving her the best closing credentials if the front-runner tires.|
runners_data.comment: Shes Got The Blues won back-to-back races before finishing third last time out, and she has experience over today's trip and going, making her a genuine threat carrying 130 lb from stall 5; the 41-day gap is the main query.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and is held up, with placed efforts at 7f on Good and Stanmore making the trip and ground combination acceptable; Mikkel Mortensen also claims 5lb, and a run 23 days ago means fair freshness, but a form string of 324664 trending in the wrong direction makes this a watching brief at best.|
runners_data.comment: Superstorm has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 61 puts him firmly in contention from stall 7 with 23 days between runs suggesting he arrives fresh — the risk is he's winless in his last six starts, and the top pair must be overcome.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Won once and placed three times in eleven similar-going starts, giving her a respectable record on fast ground; though a genuine hold-up type in her natural role, the crowded rear means she has been pushed forward on the map — David Probert's quality handling could help her find a workable position mid-race, but the style-fit discount (0.93) is real and the 13-day return is short for this yard's recent 4/18 strike rate.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a third two runs back the sole bright spot in a largely disappointing recent record, Arvana Belle at least has experience over today's distance and going and arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Carries a warning flag for fading in the finish and her form string of 00-086 tells its own story — a true hold-up type remapped to midfield given the crowded closers' group, and with only two of five similar-going runs resulting in placed finishes and zero wins, the 38-day absence adds another question mark; Molly Gunn claims 5lb but this combination faces an uphill task against the pace shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and our figures ranking her last of seven here, Snow Day faces a stiff ask — though she has run over today's trip before and a 38-day break could mean she returns fresher.

races.paceDynamic: King Cherry is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's 7f. The seven-runner field is heavily weighted toward hold-up types — Shes Got The Blues, Superstorm, Arvana Belle, and Snow Day all want to come from off the pace — meaning King Cherry faces zero front-end pressure and can set whatever tempo suits. Brighton's undulating, turning track with its stiff uphill finish rewards horses who travel into the race with cover and strike at the right moment, but a lone leader controlling fractions is notoriously hard to peg back if they are allowed a soft lead. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Snow Day and Arvana Belle are true closers forced into midfield representation, with Pennine Way and Solar Phoenix the most likely to actually secure prominent tracking positions behind King Cherry.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry establishes an uncontested lead and dictates a comfortable gallop, allowing it to conserve energy for Brighton's uphill finish.
scenarios.body: King Cherry, freed from any pressure, can coast through the early fractions and still hold a decisive advantage turning for home on the stamina-testing Brighton 7f; prominent trackers who travel smoothly into the race rather than chasing hard are best placed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry's lead fragments in the final two furlongs and a well-positioned tracker sweeps past before the hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: A prompt move from Pennine Way or Solar Phoenix tracking just off the leader would allow them to pounce the moment the front-runner weakens, reaching the line before closers can bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry sets a stronger-than-expected gallop and burns off the prominent horses, leaving a gap for the hold-up brigade to fill in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Shes Got The Blues, with a genuine recent winning profile over this course trip and similar going, is the most credible closer here, but the redistribution of Arvana Belle and Snow Day to midfield means only a true pace collapse opens this scenario reliably.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses dispute the lead early, disrupting King Cherry's rhythm and producing an unpredictable pace shape that benefits an unconsidered runner.
scenarios.body: An unexpected breakout of prominence among the hold-up types could scramble the order and produce a scrambled finish where the least fancied horse sneaks through; Superstorm, with its visored focus and prior good-ground placed efforts at 7f, is the wildcard.

watchPoints.text: King Cherry's lead is completely uncontested — watch whether Jack Doughty allows it to coast or over-quickens early; if the fractions are soft, it could prove very hard to catch on a track that already favours the leader.|

Shes Got The Blues is the form pick and has won twice at 7f on Good recently, but Myla Coppins (5lb claimer) needs to judge the run perfectly from a hold-up position — any traffic or mistimed move leaves her with too much to do up the hill.|

Arvana Belle and Snow Day are both true hold-up types compressed into midfield on the map; if they race too freely trying to find their natural position early, they risk emptying before the final furlong where Brighton's climb bites hardest.|

Solar Phoenix's 55-day absence and unknown style rating introduce genuine uncertainty about where it will travel in the race — watch the early stages to see if Dougie Costello commits to a prominent pitch or allows it to drop back, as this will determine which scenario it can influence.|
